quote: I'm pretty busy the rest of this week. They never called me on the night that they were supposed to call,
stewart_read: Customer surfaces a legitimate service complaint — a prior promised callback never happened. This is a company-caused friction point, not a scripted objection, and the schema doesn't have a named category for 'broken callback promise' specifically (closest is protocols.excessive_contact_complaint, which is TBD and not a clean match). Flagging this as a gap the schema should eventually name.
coaching_implication: Track how often customers report missed callbacks — if this recurs across calls it's an operational scheduling-reliability issue worth surfacing to Kenny, not just a one-call coaching note.

quote: Man, I'm so sorry about that. What I can do here
stewart_read: Rep apologizes directly and specifically without deflecting blame or over-explaining, then immediately pivots to the fix. This is the correct move for a service-failure complaint, though it doesn't cleanly map to empathy_on_vulnerability_disclosure since that category is scoped to health/financial/family-loss/scam disclosures, not an operational broken-promise complaint.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep could be scripted with a generic apology line rather than genuinely absorbing the complaint. Rejected — the immediacy and lack of hedging ('I'm so sorry about that') reads as a real acknowledgment, and the customer does not press further, suggesting it landed.
coaching_implication: This apology-then-fix sequence is a good模范 for other reps handling missed-callback complaints — worth flagging as a positive example if Kenny wants to build out that protocol category.

quote: Is this the best number to call? Or I see we also have your fiance's number as well. No. This number would be best.
stewart_read: A fiance's number is on file, indicating a possible co-decider, but the customer never raises the fiance as someone who needs to be part of the decision or the appointment — so protocols.spouse_decision's trigger condition (customer invoking a co-decider) was never actually met. This is better read as an unexplored qualification gap: the rep confirms which number to call but never asks whether the fiance should be included on the appointment.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may already know from the prior touch that the fiance isn't a co-owner or decision-maker, making the omission a non-issue. No evidence in this call confirms or denies that, so the gap remains open rather than resolved.
coaching_implication: When a second household member's contact info is on file, a quick 'will [fiance] be part of this decision too?' costs seconds and either confirms nothing further is needed or catches a co-decider before the specialist call.

quote: K, Gary. My name is Meg. I'm actually here with Ion Solar. How are you doing today?
stewart_read: The company name lands here, but there is no reference to why Ion has his number, no state/region anchor, and no callback to the prior design conversation until the next line. For a customer who just says 'busy right now,' a thinner legitimacy anchor makes the ask harder to land.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may be relying on the very next line (00:25, referencing the prior solar design) to carry legitimacy instead of the intro itself, effectively splitting the legitimacy anchor across two lines. This is plausible given the call is a re-engagement, not a cold open.
coaching_implication: On recontact calls, consider folding the 'why I'm calling' context into the very first breath rather than two lines later — for a busy customer, the delay costs attention.

quote: I'll go ahead and, get everything switched over and scheduled.
stewart_read: The rep books the day/time and confirms the callback number, but never runs the full button-up: no one-hour block mention, no no-driving/computer instruction, no explicit 'is that fair?' handshake. The close is functional but thin.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: this is a specialist phone call, not an in-person or online-design review appointment, so the no-driving/computer language may not apply the same way. Even so, no handshake confirmation was used at all, which the schema treats as predictive of show rate regardless of appointment type.
coaching_implication: Add a one-line handshake ('Does Monday at 6 work for you?' or similar) even on quick reschedule calls — it's the cheapest insurance against no-shows and takes only a few seconds.
